question.prompt: There is a unique sequence of integers \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(a_3,\ldots,a_{2023}\) such that \[ \begin{gathered} \tan 2023x\\ {}=\tiny\dfrac{a_1\tan x+a_3\tan^3 x+a_5\tan^5 x+\cdots+a_{2023}\tan^{2023}x}{1+a_2\tan^2 x+a_4\tan^4 x+\cdots+a_{2022}\tan^{2022}x} \end{gathered} \] whenever \(\tan 2023x\) is defined. What is \(a_{2023}?\)

solutions.title: Read the last complex-binomial term
solutions.explanation:
The odd powers in the numerator and even powers in the denominator match the imaginary and real terms of a complex binomial expansion.

Let \(i^2=-1\). De Moivre's identity, obtained by repeatedly applying the sine and cosine addition formulas, states that
\[
(\cos x+i\sin x)^{2023}
=\cos2023x+i\sin2023x.
\]
Because \(2023\) is odd, any angle where \(\cos x=0\) also has \(\cos2023x=0\). Thus whenever the given tangent is defined, we may set \(t=\tan x\) and divide by \(\cos^{2023}x\), obtaining
\[
(1+it)^{2023}
=\frac{\cos2023x+i\sin2023x}{\cos^{2023}x}.
\]
Write the binomial expansion on the left as \(R(t)+iI(t)\), where \(R\) and \(I\) have real coefficients. Even powers of \(it\) contribute to \(R\), whose constant term is \(1\); odd powers contribute to \(I\). All coefficients are integers by the binomial theorem.

Taking the ratio of imaginary to real parts gives
\[
\tan2023x=\frac{I(t)}{R(t)}.
\]
Here \(R(t)=\cos2023x/\cos^{2023}x\ne0\) on the required domain. This is a representation of exactly the stated form, so its coefficients are the given unique coefficients.

Only the final binomial term can contribute \(t^{2023}\):
\[
(it)^{2023}=i^{2023}t^{2023}
=i^{4\cdot505+3}t^{2023}
=-it^{2023}.
\]
Thus the coefficient in \(I(t)\) is \(a_{2023}=\boxed{-1}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutions.title: Track the coefficient by angle addition
solutions.explanation:
The tangent addition formula builds each multiple-angle expression from the previous one. We can use it to track the highest coefficient without finding the other coefficients.

Set \(t=\tan x\), and start with polynomials \(P_1(t)=t\), \(Q_1(t)=1\). The formula
\[
\tan((n+1)x)=\frac{\tan nx+\tan x}{1-\tan nx\tan x}
\]
suggests the polynomial recurrences
\[
P_{n+1}=P_n+tQ_n,
\qquad Q_{n+1}=Q_n-tP_n.
\]
Induction using sine and cosine addition verifies more precisely that
\[
P_n(t)=\frac{\sin nx}{\cos^n x},
\qquad Q_n(t)=\frac{\cos nx}{\cos^n x}
\]
whenever \(\cos x\ne0\). Thus \(P_n/Q_n=\tan nx\) wherever both sides are defined, without requiring intermediate tangents to be defined.

The recurrences preserve integer coefficients, give \(Q_n(0)=1\), and show that \(P_n\) has only odd powers while \(Q_n\) has only even powers. Neither polynomial has degree greater than \(n\).

Applying the recurrence twice gives
\[
P_{n+2}=(1-t^2)P_n+2tQ_n.
\]
For odd \(n\), let \(c_n\) be the coefficient of \(t^n\) in \(P_n\). Since \(Q_n\) has only even powers and degree at most \(n\), its degree is at most \(n-1\). Therefore \(2tQ_n\) has degree at most \(n\), and the only contribution to \(t^{n+2}\) is from \(-t^2P_n\). Hence
\[
c_{n+2}=-c_n.
\]
Starting from \(c_1=1\), there are \((2023-1)/2=1011\) sign reversals, so
\[
c_{2023}=(-1)^{1011}=-1.
\]
For this odd multiple, \(\cos2023x\ne0\) ensures \(\cos x\ne0\), and the displayed formulas ensure \(Q_{2023}(t)\ne0\). Thus these polynomials give the required representation on its entire stated domain. Their parity and denominator constant term match the prescribed form, so uniqueness identifies \(a_{2023}=c_{2023}=\boxed{-1}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
